hyps.why: Very large learning rates diverge, so stepping down recovers large accuracy.
Increasing an already-large learning rate worsens divergence.
Tiny learning rates under-train in 243 epochs, so raising them helps.
Deeper nets are less stable at high learning rates.
Shallower nets are more stable at high learning rates.
Narrower layers reduce the instability of large-step training.
Already strong L2 regularization underfits further when increased.
Relaxing excessive L2 penalty reduces underfitting.
Smaller batches give more updates and noise tolerance, helping at high learning rates.
With small learning rates, wider layers learn faster and help.
